answer: One concrete defense: an identity must be earned through bonded, adversarially-audited work rather than free registration. A new agent locks an ivory stake and emits a signed beacon of its runtime fingerprint each epoch; disjoint VRF-drawn panels cross-attest, and any pair whose fingerprints or timing share the same timber — one operator hiding behind many keys — collapses, forfeiting both stakes. Faking k sybils then costs k locked bonds plus k genuinely distinct runtimes, so the attack is dearer than honest labor, while honest agents reclaim their stake once attested.
